case.case_title: Abeyaratne v Janatha Fertilizer Enterprises Ltd. and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [2003] 1 Sri L.R 391

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the termination of the petitioner’s services without an inquiry violated his rights under Article 12(1) of the Constitution, specifically regarding equality before the law and equal protection.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his termination without an inquiry was arbitrary, capricious, and violated his fundamental rights under Article 12(1), including denial of natural justice and unequal treatment.
key_facts: The petitioner was Finance Manager of a government-owned company appointed in 1996.
In 2000, the 2nd respondent accused the petitioner of mismanagement and requested explanations.
Despite the petitioner’s detailed explanation, the 2nd respondent terminated his services without a charge sheet or inquiry.
The petitioner had previously received commendation for his work and had introduced a new sales procedure that was unfavorably viewed by the 2nd respondent.
The termination was alleged to be motivated by ill will and harassment by the 2nd and 3rd respondents.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equality before the law and equal protection, which includes the right to a fair hearing before termination of employment. Denial of natural justice and arbitrary actions infringe this constitutional right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that terminating the petitioner without an inquiry or charge sheet was arbitrary and capricious, violating the petitioner’s right to equal protection under Article 12(1). The evidence of ill will and harassment further supported the violation.
principles_established: Termination of employment without a fair hearing violates Article 12(1).
Even if allegations against an employee are serious, the right to be heard must be respected.
Arbitrary and capricious actions by authorities infringe constitutional equality rights.
precedents_cited: General Medical Council v Spackman (1943) AC 627
Amaradasa v Land Reform Commission 79 NLR 505
Coopers/ The Wandsworth Board of Works 14 C.B. (NS) 180
Izadeen v The Director General of Civil Aviation (1996) 2 Sri LR 348
W. P. C. Fernando v Milk Industries of Lanka Company Ltd. SC 670/97

outcome.holding: The court held that the termination without inquiry was contrary to natural justice, arbitrary, capricious, and infringed the petitioner’s rights under Article 12(1).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court’s reasoning as it protects the petitioner’s right to equality before the law and equal protection, which was violated by the arbitrary termination without a fair hearing.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The termination of the petitioner’s services without an inquiry was contrary to natural justice, arbitrary and capricious and infringed the petitioner’s rights under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
